runners_data.name: Varzi
runners_data.note: Two-year-old from the Burke yard (13/42 in 14 days) who has only run over 5-6f, making this 7f debut on soft ground a significant question mark; midfield style suits the pace shape but he is very much unexposed over the trip.

runners_data.name: Kach Above
runners_data.note: Three wins from his last three 7f starts and drawn in the most favoured stall (1), Loughnane's colt has established strong credentials at this trip on good ground — soft is a minor query but the low draw compensates and he is a big player.

runners_data.name: Dandyman Dan
runners_data.note: Strand danger identified by the scorecard; prominent racer from stall 6 (neutral draw) who has struggled on soft previously (9th at 6f soft), so today's conditions are a real concern despite his solid otherwise form, and Kevin Stott will need to find a smooth passage.

runners_data.name: Engraved
runners_data.note: Only one run to his name — a 2nd over 1m on good — so stepping back to 7f and handling soft ground are both unknown quantities; Fanshawe's colt is prominent in style and Muscutt will look to track the leader, but this is very much a watch-and-learn exercise.

runners_data.name: Forbidden Fire
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for the in-form Balding yard on a horse who won on debut over 6f on good, but stall 8 is against him (unfavoured draw) and neither soft ground nor this longer trip has been tested; the talent is there but the unknowns are stacking up.

runners_data.name: Rock Montreal
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's once-raced winner over 7f on good — the trip is right — but stall 7 (against), soft ground untested, and this is a significant step up in class for a horse on a single run; Ray Dawson partners and the upside exists but it is priced into the wider market.

runners_data.name: Nabati
runners_data.note: Strand top pick; William Buick rides for the all-powerful Appleby-Godolphin operation and this horse's OR of 104 towers over the field — his hold-up style from a neutral draw is tailor-made for the pace shape Vega King creates, and his 1-2-1 form shows he handles pressure well.

runners_data.name: Minkaas
runners_data.note: A hold-up type stepping up from 6f wins, drawn wide in stall 9 (against) and partnered by Marquand for a small yard (0/4 in 14 days); the soft ground is another unknown, and fighting from an outside draw against classier rivals makes this very tough.

runners_data.name: Vega King
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner from a favoured draw (stall 2) who will dictate every yard of this race; his form figure of 0 (last of 10 over 7f good) is concerning, but that came in a different context and Burke's yard is firing — soft ground and a clear lead could flatter him significantly.

races.paceDynamic: Vega King is the sole confirmed front-runner and, drawn in stall 2 (favoured), will stride comfortably to the lead from the off without a single rival capable of matching his early foot — this is a one-horse pace scenario. With Dandyman Dan and Engraved likely to settle in prominent positions just behind, the gallop will be honest but controlled rather than suicidal, given Vega King has no one to fight with for the lead on soft ground over 7f. Nabati (Strand top) and Kach Above will settle in midfield to hold-up positions, needing the pace to be sustained enough to draw on their finishing kicks in the straight. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a measured but genuine gallop on soft ground — favours horses who can travel smoothly in behind and then sustain their effort through the testing final furlong, giving the edge decisively to hold-up and midfield closers with proven stamina and class.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Vega King Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Vega King leads at his own pace and the soft ground ensures stamina is the deciding factor in the straight.
scenarios.body: Vega King sets an honest but uncontested tempo that strings the field out on soft ground, and as he ties up inside the final 2f, the classier hold-up horses sweep through; Nabati's powerful finishing kick over this course and distance suits this shape perfectly, and Kach Above — proven over 7f on good — can also make late headway from a favoured draw.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively steady and Vega King's rivals fail to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: A moderate early gallop on soft ground can paradoxically help the lone front-runner, as the horses in behind never build the momentum to reel him in; Vega King, trained by the in-form Burke yard (13/42 in 14 days), bounced back with a win over further and could prove harder to catch than his recent form figure suggests.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and a horse close to the leader nips through on the inside along the favoured low draw.
scenarios.body: Dandyman Dan, positioned prominently from a neutral draw with Stott in the saddle, could benefit if the closers are held up slightly too long and the low-draw rail run opens; his Strand scorecard danger tag reflects a profile that suits a race run at a pace that flattens out the high-class finishers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the going deteriorates further and soft-ground specialists outperform their ratings on a testing surface.
scenarios.body: Rock Montreal and Minkaas are both lightly raced and unproven in this company, but at big prices they could outrun market expectations if the ground tests stamina harder than anticipated; this remains the least-likely shape given the class of Nabati and the structured pace map.

watchPoints.text: Dandyman Dan's soft-ground record (0 wins, 0 places from 1 run on soft) is a live worry on today's going — if he struggles to travel sweetly behind Vega King, his Strand danger tag may not materialise.

Stall 9 (Minkaas) and stall 8 (Forbidden Fire) are drawn against the favoured low side — both will need significant early position changes to race competitively, and on soft ground that extra ground cost is amplified.

Kach Above's trainer David Loughnane has recorded 0 wins from 20 runners in the last 14 days — while the horse's draw and form are strong, the yard's current form cycle is a factor to weigh before assuming market confidence.

The going report shows Good To Soft across all races — this is softer than the listed "Soft" in the race conditions — if the going is genuinely on the better side of expectations, Vega King's hold on the lead becomes even more pronounced and Nabati's powerful late kick becomes slightly less certain to be needed.

Engraved steps back from 1m to 7f for Fanshawe — a trainer who tends to improve horses with experience — but with only one run and a neutral draw, Muscutt's ability to find a prominent position behind Vega King early will be key to whether this colt is a factor at all.

runners_data.name: Nyman
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 7f on Soft and has placed twice over this mile trip in similar conditions; drawn 9 (neutral) and races from midfield, giving him a chance if the pace is honest enough to play into his late run.

runners_data.name: Masaban
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard's top selection at low confidence; front-runner who has a mile win on Good ground and placed on Soft, and with 34 days off he arrives fresh for Edward Bethell, though he must repel Clatford from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose form string reads as a sequence of fourths and fifths — consistent but not winning — drawn 6 (neutral) and races from midfield; the Good To Soft conditions are fine but this horse needs rivals to capitulate rather than showing a decisive turn of foot.

runners_data.name: Bella Bisbee
runners_data.note: Prominent racer drawn in the favoured stall 5 on the left side of the course, and her second from stall 7 over 7f on Good ground shows she handles placed racing well; Scott Dixon's 0/20 over 14 days is a slight negative for the trainer.

runners_data.name: Celtic Chariot
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard danger; drawn ideally in stall 1 (favoured) and has back-to-back wins over this mile trip on Good ground, giving her strong course-and-distance form credentials that make her a natural threat to Masaban off a 27-day break.

runners_data.name: Clatford
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner drawn in favoured stall 2 but returns after an 85-day absence, which is a notable fitness question for Scott Dixon whose trainer strike rate over 14 days is 0/20; if he fails to fire early, the pace dynamic changes significantly.

runners_data.name: Little Miss India
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who arrives after a 140-day absence and whose recent form is over 10f and 12f — this mile trip is likely to be on the sharp side; Gary Bardwell takes the ride, and the headgear entry (h) may help sharpen her focus.

runners_data.name: Espona Bay
runners_data.note: Prominently-raced three-year-old with a win over 7f on Good ground but drawn in stall 15 (against), which is a clear disadvantage on this track where low draws are favoured; Scott Dixon runner with the same 0/20 trainer concern.

runners_data.name: Wield
runners_data.note: Three-year-old midfield racer who wore a tongue-tie last time and has placed twice over this trip; drawn in stall 3 (favoured), which is a positive, though the 0/7 trainer stat for Joseph Parr over 14 days offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Shadow Run
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse by style but squeezed to midfield on the map because the field is stacked with rear-of-field types; his most recent run over this trip on Soft produced a sixth, and racing in a position closer than ideal means his chance is tempered by a style-fit penalty.

runners_data.name: Serious Look
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse whose form is built around staying trips of 10f and 12f on AW surfaces — dropping to a mile on turf is a significant shift, and although he won at 8f, the conditions and trip combination here look against him.

runners_data.name: Caragio
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced hold-up type who has been off 89 days; has winning form over 6f on Good ground but is drawn in stall 11 (against) and stepping up slightly in stamina terms relative to his best form, making this a speculative assignment.

runners_data.name: Tolstoy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse with headgear and a poor recent sequence (-54000) who has been beaten a long way in recent starts; the Good To Soft conditions are flagged as a concern by his sim-going record (1/8), and this profile is hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Anthropologist
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who wore a hood (p) last time and has placed at 7f on Soft and Standard, with a two-placed run at 7f on a similar surface; drawn 8 (neutral) and is consistent without threatening to win, though Michael Herrington is in form at 3/18 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Quiet Resolve
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with placed form on Good to Soft and Good ground over a mile, drawn in stall 16 (against), which is the most significant negative here; Gay Kelleway takes the ride, and despite the form, the draw makes finding cover and getting across expensive in a 16-runner field.

runners_data.name: Feel The Need
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by inclination who is effectively mapped closer to midfield because the rear is too congested; the 0/8 sim-going strike rate and a recent sequence of -20067 make this a very difficult profile to back, even if the pace scenario were ideal.

races.paceDynamic: Clatford and Masaban are both confirmed front-runners drawn in stalls 2 and 10 respectively, and they will contest the early lead from the outset, creating a genuinely contested gallop on Good To Soft ground over a mile at Doncaster. With both horses committed to racing prominently, the pace should be honest rather than suicidal, but neither is likely to surrender without a fight, meaning the tempo will be sustained enough to test stamina. Celtic Chariot and Bella Bisbee, both drawn in the favoured low numbers, will look to track the pace from a prominent position, putting them in an ideal tactical spot if the front-runners begin to tighten late. This race shape — a competitive but not ruinous pace — marginally favours prominent racers drawn low who can sit just off the lead and pounce, rather than either pure front-runners or deep closers; the field holds more hold-up and prominent types than can all secure their preferred positions, and Shadow Run and Feel The Need, both genuine hold-up horses, have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they are unlikely to find clear running from the rear in a 16-runner field with this much pace pressing forward.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Clatford and Masaban fight for the lead and set an honest gallop that strings the field out, rewarding those who track them from close quarters.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners ensure a genuine tempo that will expose any weaknesses in stamina on Good To Soft ground, and prominent horses drawn in the favoured low numbers will be ideally placed to pounce as the leaders tire in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Masaban escapes Clatford's challenge early and establishes a clear lead, controlling the pace and quickening on his own terms.
scenarios.body: Masaban has winning form on soft ground and has already shown he can make all over a mile, and if Clatford fails to press him from stall 2 — whether through a slow break or a tactical decision from Jimmy Quinn — Masaban could coast to victory in the manner the Strand Scorecard identifies.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough between Clatford and Masaban to dramatically increase the stamina demands, triggering a gruelling finish on tiring ground.
scenarios.body: With 16 runners and Good To Soft conditions, a truly contested early duel could see both front-runners come back to the field, opening the race up for a horse with superior stamina and a strong late finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Shadow Run and Feel The Need to midfield backfires and the true hold-up horses cannot find a clear run, leaving the race to a late-charging but less fancied type.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely scenario given both redistributed hold-up types are effectively racing out of role and the draw favours those racing prominently from low stalls, meaning genuine closers are tactically compromised before the start.

watchPoints.text: Celtic Chariot is drawn in stall 1 (favoured) with back-to-back mile wins — if she tracks the pace cleanly, she is the most dangerous horse to Masaban's lead.
Clatford's 85-day absence is a major flag in a front-runner — if he misses the break or lacks early pace, the entire race shape changes and Masaban gets a free lead.
The Scott Dixon stable has a 0/20 strike rate over the last 14 days across Clatford, Espona Bay and Bella Bisbee — monitor for any market moves or late jockey changes as a health-of-yard signal.

Shadow Run and Feel The Need are genuine hold-up types forced into midfield by the volume of closers in this race — if the pace collapses or the field bunches, they could become traffic problems for horses immediately behind them.

Stalls 13–16 (Feel The Need, Quiet Resolve, Espona Bay, Serious Look) are all drawn against the favoured rail — any of these runners will need to overcome a structural disadvantage regardless of form.

runners_data.note: Won last time out over 5f on Soft (sim-going record 1W1P), which is directly relevant here; Oisin Murphy in the saddle adds confidence, and draw 1 is neutral on this flat track — likely to race prominently just off the pace-setters in a perfect stalking position.

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien give this horse the strongest jockey-trainer combination in the race; OR 112 is the highest in the field, but soft-going sim-form shows 0W1P and recent form 291742 includes several disappointing efforts — needs to bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: In The Black
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 5f on Good and has genuine front-running inclinations, but this field is too pace-rich for that position to be available — pushed back into midfield on the map, it will likely find itself racing in an unnatural role, which tempers confidence in its prospects despite the OR gap to leaders.

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: Natural midfield type with a solid recent run of 3rd on Good to Soft over 6f; Daniel Tudhope is a strong course jockey and 21 days since last run is fine — suited by a genuine gallop that sets up a sustained finish but needs the pace collapse scenario to materialise.

runners_data.name: Final Objective
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard top selection at OR 107 with recent course-winning form; James Doyle rides and the horse is a genuine front-runner with a soft-ground run (2nd) in its last start — will go straight to the front and sets the pace shape for the entire race.

runners_data.name: Crownbreaker
runners_data.note: OR 97 and prominent style, but recent form string 325107 shows a blow-out last time on soft over 6f — stepping back to 5f is the right call, and David Egan knows this track, though the trainer's T14 strike rate of 4/18 is the best angle here.

runners_data.name: Flann Sunna
runners_data.note: 43-day absence is the biggest concern; won two on the bounce before a 5th, has only run on Good ground in the hist, and William Buick's booking is an obvious positive — needs to handle the softer conditions first time out after the break.

runners_data.name: Tokaido
runners_data.note: Carries a fade-in-finish warning flag which is a significant negative in any scenario; the only soft-ground run produced a 16th over 6f, and a hold-up style does not suit a race with genuine front-running pace — Amy Murphy's yard is in fair form but this runner faces structural problems.

runners_data.name: Fast Track
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner who will push Final Objective throughout the early stages; headgear (t) listed, and the horse has been placed in four of its last five, all on Good — zero soft-ground experience is a real question mark on today's ground, potentially the critical factor.

runners_data.name: El Floridita
runners_data.note: Wears a visor (v) and runs in midfield; a winner last time out over 5f on Good and second on soft in the hist — Nigel Tinkler has modest T14 numbers, but Rowan Scott is capable and the horse has the profile to benefit if the pace truly burns.

runners_data.name: Pershaada
runners_data.note: OR 106 and prominent style; soft-ground sim record 0W0P from six runs is a nagging concern despite being a dual winner on Good — form 321410 is patchy and the trainer Hannon angle is workable but this needs a better going profile to inspire full confidence.

runners_data.name: Ronson
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type and a 5f winner on Good last time; soft-going sim-form is 0W0P from five runs which is a worry, and Alex Jary is an apprentice claim rider — needs the most extreme pace scenario and clean ground to find a run from the back.

races.paceDynamic: Final Objective and Fast Track are the two confirmed front-runners and will immediately contest the lead from stalls opening, creating a genuine, honest gallop down Doncaster's straight five — on Good to Soft ground that will test stamina as well as speed, this is unlikely to be a dawdle. With five of twelve runners wanting a prominent position, the early stages will be congested and competitive, compressing the midfield and potentially creating traffic issues two to three furlongs out as the field fans across the track. That contested pace on a softened surface classically brings the race back to prominent runners who can track the leaders without over-committing, allowing them to pick off exhausted front-runners in the final furlong — this race shape most favours a handy, prominent-style horse with tactical speed to latch onto the pace and finish past it. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Final Objective and Fast Track are most likely to actually lead, with Sale Shark, Carry The Flag, and Flann Sunna fighting for the next tier immediately behind them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Final Objective and Fast Track fight up front and burn each other out, allowing a close-tracking prominent to pounce.
scenarios.body: The honest early gallop set by two genuine front-runners on Good to Soft ground will drain reserves, leaving the race to a horse that races prominently without wasting energy in the lead battle; the soft ground amplifies this dynamic by punishing pace-setters further.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters — most likely Final Objective — establishes a commanding lead and the field fails to close the gap.
scenarios.body: A fast-starting leader who dictates an uncontested or lightly-contested gallop can time-trial away from the field on a straight five; Final Objective has the class edge at OR 107 and the Strand Scorecard marks it as top selection, making this a meaningful alternative outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Finishers
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace is fierce enough to compromise all prominent runners and the race opens up for midfielders to reel them in.
scenarios.body: Agamemnon and El Floridita, both natural midfield-style runners, would benefit most if the pace burns through the prominent group; their ability to travel wide of trouble and produce a sustained finish suits this shape, though this scenario requires a more extreme pace collapse than is typical.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a strong enough gallop from front to back that genuine hold-up horses can reel in the field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Ronson and Tokaido sit furthest back and would need exceptional pace from the front runners combined with a clear run — Tokaido carries a fade flag that makes this unlikely, while Ronson's form at 5f on soft gives marginal hope; this is the least probable shape given the field's authentic pace dynamic.

watchPoints.text: Fast Track has no recorded soft-ground experience — if the going tests its stamina, it may capitulate after half a furlong and surrender the lead entirely to Final Objective, reshaping the whole dynamic.

Prominent congestion from Sale Shark, Carry The Flag, Flann Sunna, and Crownbreaker all chasing the same position means a pocket or squeeze two furlongs out is a genuine risk for any horse on the inside — draw positioning will be critical.
Flann Sunna returns after 43 days off and has never encountered soft ground in five career starts — William Buick's fitness confidence will need to be trusted on faith rather than evidence.

Tokaido's fade flag combined with a hold-up style and a soft-ground 16th on the only soft run makes it a horse to watch for early traffic disruption rather than any winning prospect — monitor its position at halfway.

Final Objective's trainer Hamad Al Jehani has a modest T14 record of 2/10 but this horse's profile — Strand top pick, front-runner, soft-ground second — means the race shape is built around it regardless of stable form.

runners_data.name: Caballo De Mar
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner, drawing well enough in stall 6 to press forward; Oisin Murphy is the significant booking and soft-going form holds up, but a finishing-fade flag and OR 115 in a Group 2 staying test raise doubts about whether he can sustain his advantage — best viewed as the pace-maker who shapes the race rather than wins it.

runners_data.name: Winday
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the mount for Emmet Mullins on this lightly-raced three-year-old whose sole win came on good ground over 12f — naturally a pace-pressing type but the field density means he is unlikely to get close to the front, and a career-high trip on soft ground adds significant uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Queenstown
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this six-year-old who most recently won on good ground over 14f, and the combination of a top jockey, prominent racing style, and Ballydoyle team form (T14: 5/34) makes him the one best-placed to travel close to the pace and deliver a clean challenge; soft-going sim record shows one place from three, a mild concern but the overall profile is strong.

runners_data.name: Epic Poet
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old veteran for David O'Meara who races from midfield and has mixed soft-ground form (one placing from five sim-going runs) — form string of 534650 is not encouraging, and at OR 107 he is likely to find the top of this field beyond him unless the race fragments chaotically.

runners_data.name: Peace Belle
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides this hold-up mare who has placed twice in soft conditions in her last five runs, so the going is not a concern; she goes from a handy draw in stall 5 and her strongest form comes when the race becomes a genuine stamina test, making her the most credible late-closer if conditions bite hard.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee partners this six-year-old whose recent soft-ground form (4/12 overall in sim-going) is modest, and OR 101 makes him an outsider in Group 2 class; natural hold-up style means he needs a strongly-run race to produce his best, which this shape may not deliver.

runners_data.name: Ascending
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old whose recent form reads 6-7064 and who fades in finishes — naturally a pace-prominent type but pushed back by the density of prominent runners in this field; the style-fit flag (0.94) underlines that racing out of his comfort zone materially reduces his chance, and the soft ground does not bolster his claims.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Sundance
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's six-year-old returns after 42 days off — the longest absence in the field — having won twice on standard ground over 16f; prominent racing style suits the anticipated shape and he is well drawn in stall 1, making him a genuine each-way player if freshness translates to a forward show, though soft ground is less proven for him.

races.paceDynamic: Caballo De Mar is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 2m2f Doncaster Cup, and on soft ground over a gruelling trip he is likely to dictate at a measured, controlled tempo rather than an honest gallop — a pace shape that could compress the race and suit those able to travel close to him. Berkshire Sundance and Queenstown are both natural prominent racers capable of sitting just off the lead, which means Caballo De Mar will have company rather than total isolation, but crucially neither is likely to force a truly searching pace. This field contains more front-running and prominent types than can all get their preferred position: Winday and Ascending are genuine up-with-the-pace horses but both are redistributed to midfield in this map, with Caballo De Mar and Berkshire Sundance most likely to secure the front positions ahead of Queenstown, while Winday and Ascending are forced to race further back than they would wish. The overall shape — one genuine pace-setter with a sustainable gallop on soft ground over a staying trip — favours a patient, prominent racer who can travel close to the pace without extravagant use of energy and finish with purpose, squarely pointing toward the Queenstown profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Queenstown Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Caballo De Mar sets a controlled, sustainable pace and Queenstown settles close to the lead before asserting from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Caballo De Mar's measured tempo on soft ground creates an ideal hunting ground for Queenstown, who can travel comfortably in the slipstream before Ryan Moore delivers his challenge at the right moment; the soft going rewards a strong, relentless finisher rather than a sprinter, which suits Queenstown's profile well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Caballo De Mar Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and Caballo De Mar is allowed to coast in front before kicking clear from three furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A very slow early tempo gifted entirely to the front-runner could mean Caballo De Mar builds an insurmountable advantage, with pursuing horses unable to close on a horse who has conserved energy throughout; soft ground over this trip is a concern for his stamina but a dawdling gallop could negate that worry entirely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If Caballo De Mar sets a stronger-than-expected pace and the race develops into a gruelling test of stamina in the soft, opening it up for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A genuine staying test in the soft ground would suit Peace Belle and Beylerbeyi, who are natural hold-up types with course form in similar conditions and have the stamina profiles to grind home late; the caveat is that the pace currently mapped suggests this is not the most likely shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Horse Fires
scenarios.trigger: If Winday or Ascending breaks free from the traffic and manages to secure an uncontested prominent position despite the field dynamics.
scenarios.body: Both are natural front-runners or prominent racers whose true pace preferences are masked by the redistribution, and if either secures a cleaner berth than expected they could travel into the race with minimal effort; however, both carry style-fit discounts and their form in this type of trip and going gives limited grounds for confidence.

watchPoints.text: Queenstown — watch whether Ryan Moore elects to sit tight behind Caballo De Mar from the outset rather than trying to match him stride for stride, as that patient prominent ride is the trigger for the most likely winning scenario.

Winday and Ascending — both are genuine pace-pressing types who cannot get their natural position; monitor in the first half-mile for signs of riders forcing the issue, which would increase the overall pace and fundamentally alter the race shape.

Caballo De Mar — the finishing-fade flag is live over this trip in soft ground; if he is still in front entering the final two furlongs he has over-performed his expected role, but if pursued from three out he is vulnerable to being swallowed up.

Peace Belle — soft-ground form holds up in sim-going and she is the truest hold-up runner in the field; only relevant if the race is run at a thorough gallop, so track the early sectionals to assess whether this shape can develop.

Berkshire Sundance — the 42-day absence is the key variable for this trainer whose 14-day strike rate (12/58) suggests horses leave the yard in good order; if he comes forward fresh he could press Caballo De Mar and complicate the pace picture.

runners_data.name: Silver Lake
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for William Haggas and James Doyle who has won three of her last four including twice on soft — the step up to 1m4f from 1m2f is a logical progression for this improving filly, and her pattern of finishing strongly makes a genuinely contested gallop ideal.

runners_data.name: Salamanca City
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's five-year-old has winning form at 1m2f and 1m4f on soft and good-to-soft, and Daniel Muscutt should be able to slot her comfortably into midfield; three placed efforts from six runs on similar going suggests she handles conditions but hasn't always converted.

runners_data.name: Green Sky
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's hold-up mare carries only 128lbs and holds proven form at 1m4f on soft, with three wins over the trip on good or better and a placed run on soft last time — the Scorecard's selection and Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim helps with the weight, though she has not won on genuinely soft going.

runners_data.name: Room Fourteen
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's three-year-old has a strong form record at 1m2f but steps up significantly in trip here — all five of her recent starts have been at 1m2f or shorter, so the stamina question over 1m4f on soft ground is real, though she is clearly in good form with Saffie Osborne booked.

runners_data.name: Ruby Wedding
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a major positive for Andrew Balding's filly, who has a win over 1m4f on good ground and ran prominently to finish second on Standard last time; she is drawn widest on the inside (stall 1) which suits a horse likely to track close to the pace from the off.

runners_data.name: Thatwilldoso
runners_data.note: Kevin Coleman's five-year-old is a prominent racer who has won twice over 1m2f on good ground and placed three times from eight tries on similar conditions — the soft underfoot queries in her history (ran tenth on soft in 2024) are a concern, and the trainer's 14-day record of 0/11 offers little confidence.

runners_data.name: Nochebuena
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is one of the two confirmed pace-setters, and her win on soft ground over 1m2f last time out shows she handles conditions — 63 days off the track is a minor query, but Beckett does well with returning horses, and she must fight off Golden Muse for the early lead.

runners_data.name: Aequitas
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old returns after 307 days off — a significant absence flag — and her form before the break included disappointing efforts at this sort of distance on soft ground, making her very hard to trust here despite Daniel Tudhope retaining the ride.

runners_data.name: Golden Muse
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's three-year-old is the other confirmed front-runner, and David Egan will look to use her prominent style from stall 10; all four of her wins have come on Standard ground at Chelmsford, so the switch to soft turf at Doncaster after 93 days off represents a substantial stepping-stone test she must prove she can handle.

runners_data.name: Bint Al Daar
runners_data.note: The six-year-old drops significantly in class off OR 70, but her recent form string of 1-5-8-7-9-0 makes it hard to construct a positive case — Joanna Mason rides and she handles various conditions, but she has not placed in any of her last six starts and the going flag is a further concern.

races.paceDynamic: Nochebuena and Golden Muse are the two confirmed front-runners, and with both horses likely to want to be on or near the lead, the early stages over this 1m4f trip on Good To Soft ground at Doncaster should produce a genuine, contested gallop rather than a dawdled affair. Nochebuena (Jason Hart, Ralph Beckett) has led and won over soft ground before, while Golden Muse (David Egan, Marco Botti) has been prominent in all her wins; neither looks likely to concede lead without a fight, meaning the pace should be honest from the outset and the fractions will be real. The resulting tempo over this stamina-testing trip on soft-ish ground will gradually drain the front-runners, setting up the race for those who can be covered up in midfield or come from just off the pace with a sustained staying effort in the home straight. This race shape firmly favours hold-up and midfield-to-late runners who have the stamina to pick up the pieces — horses like Silver Lake and Green Sky, who settle well and stay on powerfully, are ideally positioned to benefit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Genuine Gallop, Stayers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Nochebuena and Golden Muse set a true, unrelenting pace that stretches the field and rewards genuine staying ability in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up through the soft ground, leaving the race wide open turning in for those who have been dropped in behind and conserved energy; the stamina-laden horses who settle in midfield and grind relentlessly to the line are the biggest beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Muse or Nochebuena establishes a clear lead quickly and is allowed to control a moderate enough tempo to have reserves left in the tank.
scenarios.body: One front-runner asserts immediately and the other is unable or unwilling to force a true battle, producing a steadier early pace that flatters the leader's stamina and makes it hard for hold-up horses to pick up; the horse that gets away cleanly and settles into a rhythm in front runs rivals ragged down the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine but not brutal, allowing a prominent tracker to lob just behind the leaders and produce the decisive move two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Horses like Ruby Wedding and Thatwilldoso, travelling with the pace rather than fighting it, are positioned to pounce the moment the front-runners begin to tie up; soft ground rewards those who conserve fractionally rather than grinding through every furlong from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel between Nochebuena and Golden Muse is exceptionally fierce and the whole field becomes strung out, creating a truly extreme gallop that results in a wall-to-wall stayer benefiting.
scenarios.body: The race turns into a test of pure stamina and only those held up furthest off the pace remain untouched by the carnage; the hold-up horses who have been patient throughout sweep through on the bridle late, but this scenario requires an unusually dramatic collapse at the front.

watchPoints.text: Golden Muse must prove she handles soft turf — all her wins have come on Standard Chelmsford surfaces, and if the going blunts her early pace she may capitulate quickly, changing the entire shape of the race.

Aequitas returning after 307 days off is a major lay-of-the-land watch — if she is clearly backward in her coat or awkward leaving the stalls, she can be safely sidelined, but a sharp show at the start would signal she is ready to go.

If neither Nochebuena nor Golden Muse can be restrained in the early stages and they trade seriously fierce fractions over soft ground, the race may suit an extreme hold-up finisher rather than a stalker — watch early sectionals to judge whether the pace is genuinely punishing.

Room Fourteen has never run beyond 1m2f — Saffie Osborne will need to teach her to settle and conserve on what could be a strong gallop, and any sign of pulling or racing keenly in the early stages would be a negative sign for her stamina claims.

Silver Lake's draw in stall 9 means James Doyle will need to allow the field to settle before committing to her hold-up position — on a flat, galloping track like Doncaster this is manageable, but watch whether she gets an unobstructed run into the straight or gets blocked behind the pack.

runners_data.name: It Dunt Marra
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with a recent second on soft and a win on good, but only one crack at 6f on soft (ninth) suggests the trip in these conditions may stretch her stamina; Stevie Donohoe hold from draw 4 gives her a decent position without fighting for it.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Toledo
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald takes over on this Clive Cox-trained front-runner who won over 6f on good but has only one soft run to his name; will likely go hard from the front from draw 8 and faces the question of whether he can sustain that into the ground.

runners_data.name: Bear Lee
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's hold-up filly is the Strand Scorecard's primary danger, with genuine soft form and a recent run just 11 days ago keeping her sharp; from draw 1 Joanna Mason will need a seam to open late, but a strong gallop ahead of her plays directly into her profile.

runners_data.name: Washington Royale
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's filly won on soft over 6f last time out from draw 9, which is exactly the profile this scenario rewards; Clifford Lee can sit just off the pace and she has a strong recent record in similar conditions, making her a credible beneficiary of a fast-run race.

runners_data.name: Baddaddan
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes the ride on this Richard Spencer-trained runner who won over 6f on good; has posted a big run in that form (14th at 6f good also on record) so consistency is a question, but the prominent style and draw 14 give him room to manoeuvre.

runners_data.name: Super Tuscan
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's runner has a win on good and has finished second over 6f good most recently; Oliver Carmichael (7lb) is a notable allowance claim but the horse's form on firmer ground raises a mild query about whether Good To Soft fully suits.

runners_data.name: Henley On Thames
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's Strand Scorecard selection has won twice over 6f on good and finished second twice more; David Egan is a major booking and the progressive form string (62211) suggests a horse finding its feet at exactly the right time, with the prominent style ideal for tracking a fast early pace.

runners_data.name: Launch Sequence
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke sends out this well-credentialed midfield type with James Doyle aboard and a form string of 336 that suggests consistent placed efforts without winning; the headgear flag and soft-going form (sixth at 7f soft last time) are worth monitoring as the going may not be his best.

runners_data.name: Tumishi
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's prominently-raced filly won over 6f on good 15 days ago with Daniel Muscutt aboard again; freshness and a recent win are both positives, and draw 2 is workable, though she steps up from a straightforward win into a 16-runner handicap.

runners_data.name: Wait Geordie
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's front-runner has a troubled recent record with five consecutive finishes of 3-8-7-8-5, all on good going over 5f; the step up to 6f on soft is a significant shift in conditions, and 37 days off adds uncertainty about whether this is a revival or a continuation of a poor run.

runners_data.name: Beresford Gap
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes a potentially significant booking on Andrew Balding's front-runner, whose last start was 50 days ago; showed a place effort over 6f on soft in the form string but will need to match the pace of Pride Of Toledo and others to dominate — likely to be swallowed up in the early battle.

runners_data.name: Sir Sirius
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's runner was last seen 78 days ago and his form figures (963) don't inspire confidence; from draw 13 and with Tom Eaves aboard, he is one of several front-runners who will burn energy in a pace battle he is unlikely to win.

runners_data.name: Innichen
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this Jack Channon hold-up horse who has an erratic form string including a 19th on soft last time; the one-from-seven record on soft is a concern, though his wins have come on good and the hold-up style theoretically suits a fast-run race — the soft-ground question is real.

runners_data.name: Sue's Last Chance
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's front-runner has modest figures (6-5-8-0) and is the lowest-rated confirmed pace horse in the field; the headgear flag (p) implies she will go forward, but her chance of surviving a five-way pace battle to the line looks slim.

runners_data.name: Fasthope
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's runner is a natural prominent racer by inclination — with a win over 6f on good and soft-going form in the book — but with so many pace rivals already committed to the front, she is mapped to midfield and will likely be unable to claim her preferred berth; Cam Hardie will need to adapt accordingly.

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent performer (form: 431346) is a genuine prominent type whose natural position will be squeezed out by the volume of front-runners in this field; Duran Fentiman rides from draw 16 and the horse, despite headgear (ht) and a decent record over 6f, is effectively racing out of role, which tempers the prospect.

races.paceDynamic: Five confirmed front-runners — Pride Of Toledo, Wait Geordie, Beresford Gap, Sir Sirius, and Sue's Last Chance — guarantee a fierce early gallop over 6f on Good To Soft ground at Doncaster, a combination that will stretch stamina reserves and punish anything that expends energy fighting for position. The pace will be set at a relentless tempo from the off, meaning the front of the race will likely compress and falter in the final furlong, handing the advantage to horses that can travel smoothly in the slipstream and produce a sustained late run. This race shape heavily favours prominent-to-midfield horses with genuine stamina and soft-ground credentials — those able to sit just off the frantic early pace and still find something in testing conditions. The field carries more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate: Fern Clyde and Fasthope are natural prominent racers who, with so many pace rivals already committed to the front, are highly likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield berth against their instincts and will be racing out of their preferred role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Stalkers
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners burn each other out and the race falls apart up front from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: The intense early gallop on Good To Soft ground causes the pace contingent to tie up inside the final two furlongs, allowing prominent horses that tracked at a sensible distance to sweep past the spent leaders

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survives Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast but not catastrophically so, leaving one well-positioned prominent horse with a crucial lead at the 1f pole
scenarios.body: A single prominent type that sits third or fourth early doors avoids the worst of the cavalry charge, clears the field with a decisive mid-race move, and holds on as closers run out of ground

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace truly collapses in the final 150 yards and hold-up horses get an unimpeded run through
scenarios.body: Bear Lee and Innichen, both natural hold-up types with solid soft-ground form, would time their challenge to arrive late as the field comes back to them, but they require everything to go right positionally from wide or low draws

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Defies Logic
scenarios.trigger: If Pride Of Toledo or Beresford Gap steals a decisive break and the pace scramble behind them creates chaos that limits the challenge
scenarios.body: A single front-runner dictates a controlled enough tempo that rivals expend energy fighting for position rather than tracking them, and crosses the line with an unexpected margin

watchPoints.text: Pride Of Toledo, Wait Geordie, Beresford Gap, and Sir Sirius all want to lead — watch the first furlong for a fierce battle for supremacy that could compromise all of them before halfway.

Bear Lee breaks from draw 1 and needs a clean passage from the inside — if the pace battle creates a wall across the track Joanna Mason will have to switch, costing vital lengths on Good To Soft ground.

Fern Clyde and Fasthope are both natural prominent types who cannot get their preferred position in this field — watch whether either jockey pushes forward regardless, which would add further fuel to an already compressed pace.

Innichen's soft-ground form is poor (one placing from seven attempts) — Tom Marquand will be aware, but punters should note the hold-up profile suits the race shape even if the going is a genuine question mark.

Washington Royale won on soft 11 days ago over this exact course and distance — watch whether Clifford Lee settles her just off the carnage up front, as a repeat of that performance could be enough in a field that destroys itself from the front.

runners_data.name: Almekarem
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's patient placement record demands respect; soft-going form is solid (placed at 1/9 similar ground), midfield style suits this pace scenario, and the 11-day turnaround is no concern from this yard — a genuine contender if the stamina test is as severe as the race shape suggests.

runners_data.name: Amidst The Chaos
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has shown ability at 10f on good ground but lacks a soft-going win, with limited form over this trip; the 8-day turnaround is fine, but the soft-ground query and 12f trip on this ground for the first time represent genuine unknowns.

runners_data.name: Optician
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection (low confidence flagged) but the case is real — won over 12f on soft last time out, midfield style suits a strongly-run race, and Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim sharpens the value; the 25-day fresher preparation is a positive from this yard.

runners_data.name: Without Compromise
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with decent placed form over 10f but the step to 12f on Good to Soft is untested, and a form figure of 6 last time on similar ground is a concern; Cam Hardie rides but the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 2/16 offers modest confidence.

runners_data.name: Reveur
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a going tag of UNKNOWN — lightly raced and absent for 126 days, making this a significant unknown quantity; David O'Meara and Daniel Tudhope are a strong combination but the lack of soft-ground evidence and the layoff make this a speculative entry at best.

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: Sean Levey takes over on a horse with consistent placed form at 10-11f, including a win over 10f on good; the step to 12f could be the unlock on Good to Soft, and a prominent style sits perfectly between the warring front-runners and the hold-up pack — a pragmatic each-way profile.

runners_data.name: His Finest Hour
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners a consistent placer who has twice finished second on soft and third on good-to-soft, so the going is no concern; the 14-day trainer strike rate of 0/4 is weak, and the step to 10f in the history suggests 12f is at the outer limit, but soft-ground profile is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Director's Cut
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who hasn't won since an 8f victory on standard at Southwell — a confirmed pacemaker who will help set a brutal tempo but faces questions over 12f on Good to Soft and a 74-day break; the pace he helps create is likely to benefit others more than himself.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and comes with a fades-in-finish flag — a front-runner who has been seen wilting late, with a quick 5-day turnaround and limited form beyond 8f; likely to make the running and be swamped in the closing stages, but contributes meaningfully to the pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Something Splendid
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's danger selection: won on soft over 10f last time, Tom Marquand rides for an in-form Chapple-Hyam yard (2/4 in 14 days), and soft-ground figures of 3/6 with 2 wins 2 places speak directly to this race's conditions — prominent style avoids both the pace battle and the midfield scrimmage.

runners_data.name: Newtown Duke
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a tongue-tie and two third-place finishes on soft at 12f — quietly well-suited on paper; the 90-day absence is the key risk, but Ian Williams does place horses back successfully and Clifford Lee knows this type of staying contest well.

runners_data.name: Amancio
runners_data.note: Has won twice on soft and over long trips (17f, 9f), suggesting genuine stamina and going versatility; the 75-day break is a flag, but the tongue-tie return and form of /15-31 — including a recent third at 12f — makes this a compelling profile for a gruelling stamina test if fit.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and is a confirmed front-runner who will try to make all, but has never won beyond 9f and is unproven on soft over this trip — his role is likely to be pace-setter rather than winner, and the 12-day turnaround is fine, but his effectiveness is likely to peak at 8-9f.

runners_data.name: On The Inlet
runners_data.note: Young three-year-old front-runner who won at 7f and has been placed over 8-10f, but 12f on Good to Soft is a very different proposition; likely to be prominent early and contribute to the strong pace scenario, but 12f on this ground looks like a stamina stretch.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy — the strongest jockey booking in the race — rides a three-year-old with three wins on soft at 9-10f, making the going and general conditions a near-perfect fit; the hood suggests greenness but the soft-ground record of 3W/3P from 9 runs on similar ground is outstanding, and the 13-day freshener suits.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: David Egan partners a hold-up type whose one win came on good over 8f — the form figures on soft are modest and 12f is a step into unknown territory; the 5-day turnaround is quick, and the overall picture is of a horse who is competitive on quick ground at shorter, not a guaranteed stayer on this surface.

runners_data.name: Spirit Genie
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides a hold-up type with a tongue-tie and bit — won most recently on good over 8f but has been placed on soft previously; the 37-day absence needs to be respected, and the form at 10f+ is largely disappointing, though soft-ground profile gives a slim chance in the right scenario.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Front-runner for the Tutty yard who has a win at 10f on good but form figures on soft of 5/8 with no wins — the soft going is a concern, and 12f is a step up from most of her form; likely to make the pace before fading, playing into the hands of the hold-up horses.

runners_data.name: Naples
runners_data.note: Hold-up type fitted with a hood whose best form came at 10f on soft (3rd), but recent figures include 12th and 12th — significant lows that make this a speculative runner; PJ McDonald is a quality booking but the overall form trajectory is downward and 12f on this ground is a tough ask.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Olly, On The Inlet, Director's Cut, Canvas, and Ziata all carry genuine front-running tendencies, guaranteeing a contested, hot-paced gallop from the off on this Good to Soft 1m2f Doncaster straight course. With five legitimate pace horses competing for the early lead, none will enjoy a truly uncontested front, the tempo will be relentless, and the ground — officially Good to Soft but likely testing by the evening card — will compound the stamina demands significantly. Those who burn energy fighting for position in the van are likely to pay for it in the final two furlongs, leaving the race wide open for resolute hold-up and prominent-midfield runners who can travel within themselves before unleashing a sustained finishing effort. This race shape strongly favours genuine stayers with soft-ground form who can sit off the breakneck pace and produce a late, powerful challenge — hold-up and midfield-tracking profiles are the clear tactical beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners burn each other out and the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile, allowing hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop from Highland Olly, Director's Cut, On The Inlet, Canvas, and Ziata ensures the pace is unsustainably hot, and the Good to Soft ground turns the stamina test into a gruelling slog that exposes those who raced prominently. Hold-up horses with proven soft-ground form — particularly those with strong finishing kicks — are positioned perfectly to pick up the pieces as the pacemakers fade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Leads Home
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-midfield types conserves energy early, avoids the pace battle, and sustains a run from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A horse like Something Splendid or Everyoneknowsadave, sitting just off the pace but clear of midfield scrimmaging, finds an ideal rhythm and isn't sucked into the early war — then delivers a strong, sustained run when the front-runners cry enough. Soft-ground form and a genuine mile-and-a-quarter trip suit this profile on a course that rewards those who travel sweetly through a strongly-run race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not catastrophically destructive, allowing a midfield horse with relentless stamina to grind out victory in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Optician, the Strand Scorecard's top selection, is ideally placed in this scenario — a win on soft over this trip last time, sitting midfield under Conor Whiteley, grinding out the kind of attrition finish this race shape creates on Good to Soft ground at Doncaster. Almekarem, suited to soft conditions and trained by the ever-shrewd Sir Mark Prescott, could also deliver from a neutral draw if the race falls into a rhythm that rewards relentless travellers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Honest, Front-Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner breaks clear early and the rest of the pace horses neutralise each other, allowing a sole leader to build an unassailable advantage.
scenarios.body: Director's Cut or On The Inlet would need to steal a march on their rivals and secure clean air, but with multiple legitimate front-runners in the race this scenario requires chaos among the others — an unlikely but non-zero outcome given a field of 19. Even if one does break clear, the Good to Soft ground over 1m2f makes it extremely hard to sustain a lead set at a truly fierce gallop, limiting this scenario's probability sharply.

watchPoints.text: Fans Favourite's soft-ground record (3W/3P from 9 similar-going runs) is exceptional for a race like this — Oisin Murphy's booking alongside that form profile means this runner must be taken seriously in any late-closers scenario.

Something Splendid is the Strand Scorecard's flagged danger: Tom Marquand, Chapple-Hyam in form, won on soft last time, and a prominent style that sits ideally between the pace battle and the hold-up pack — watch for a sustained challenge from the two-furlong pole.

The five front-runners (Highland Olly, On The Inlet, Director's Cut, Canvas, Ziata) will collectively set a pace that none of them may be able to sustain — watch for a pronounced fade from all five from the two-furlong pole, which will dictate the winner's profile entirely.

Reveur's 126-day absence combined with a going tag of UNKNOWN makes this one of the biggest wildcards in the race — Daniel Tudhope and David O'Meara can land gambles, so watch the market move in the final 30 minutes for any confidence signal.

Optician's Strand Scorecard top selection is flagged at low confidence — the 12f soft form is there, but the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 3/18 and the use of a 5lb claimer in a 19-runner handicap on Good to Soft means the race execution must be near-perfect for the selection to land.
